> StreamPixel is a 3-foot RGB pixel display built mainly for music. It connects to Spotify to show the current song, artist and playback progress, then switches to pixel animations when nothing is playing. I’ll also build a companion app where I can choose animations, display custom text and pixel art, adjust brightness and control what appears on the screen. Editable native CAD (Onshape): https://cad.onshape.com/documents/ff33f56b02d9867b20260f9d/w/d771c62f16da9b74f071b096/e/97cd61c99cbb00f7ac08fe59 Printed holder CAD: https://cad.onshape.com/documents/ff33f56b02d9867b20260f9d/w/d771c62f16da9b74f071b096/e/aeadc6d027d2d7d05235b7d8

## Design

### 2026-10-29: I started planning StreamPixel, a long RGB display for my desk or wall. The idea is to show pixel animations, custom text and eventually music information. I worked around three P10 panels in a row an

**6.53h**

I started planning StreamPixel, a long RGB display for my desk or wall. The idea is to show pixel animations, custom text and eventually music information. I worked around three P10 panels in a row and started the picture-frame style enclosure in Onshape. I want the electronics hidden inside, with the power cable coming out of the case.

Getting started in Onshape took some figuring out. I got stuck on selecting the rear face for the side-wall sketch and understanding how the border should extrude. The outside and inside rectangles need to stay centred so the walls have an even thickness. I also had to think about the space behind the panels, rather than just making a border that looks right from the front.

Tomorrow I want to finish the frame walls, work through the chamfer and start the back plate and mounting holes. I still need to choose the electronics and leave enough room for the power supply and cables.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/3c22a00d-16e7-4c51-9636-060f5781bcba/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-30: I continued the Onshape frame, working on the depth, side walls and the rear of the enclosure. I also worked through the screw-hole layout so the back plate and the frame can attach properly. The fram

**5.85h**

I continued the Onshape frame, working on the depth, side walls and the rear of the enclosure. I also worked through the screw-hole layout so the back plate and the frame can attach properly. The frame is meant to hold all three panels as one long display.

The chamfer was confusing and I needed to check the selected edges and faces again. I also realised that the screw holes cannot just look close in the model: the matching parts need the same hole positions. I have been going back over those details before adding more parts around them.

Tomorrow I want to work on the vents, screen retainers and the internal holders. I need to leave access for wiring and make sure the back can come off for repairs. The power supply is one of the larger things that needs to fit inside, so I do not want to use up that space with mounting features.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/35b835d7-4c43-4354-b50e-fdbe73208fe5/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-31: I worked on the parts inside and behind the frame: the panel retainers, mounting positions, ventilation and the holders for the controller and power supply. I also wanted the case to sit away from the

**4.47h**

I worked on the parts inside and behind the frame: the panel retainers, mounting positions, ventilation and the holders for the controller and power supply. I also wanted the case to sit away from the wall so the vents have somewhere to let air out.

One issue was that I could only see one screen retainer when the full display needs several supports. I needed to go over the repeated retainers and their holes, rather than leave the mounting unfinished. I also clarified the part I had been calling the battery holder: this version uses a plugged-in 5V power supply. Its holder needs to suit that supply and leave room for the wiring.

Next I want to check the complete set of parts together and sort out the manufacturing files. I need the CNC parts and printed holders clearly separated, along with the wiring schematic and a proper parts list. Actual component measurements will still be needed before fabrication.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/6620955c-3a0f-4344-af75-f46f7d84dbd6/video.mp4)

### 2026-11-01: Today was mostly checking and organising the project for the design handoff. The CNC frame, back plate and fittings are separated from the three printed pieces: the controller tray and the two power-s

**6.47h**

Today was mostly checking and organising the project for the design handoff. The CNC frame, back plate and fittings are separated from the three printed pieces: the controller tray and the two power-supply holder halves. StreamPixel and Ridith Shetty are on the frame. The CAD package has STEP files, the flat cutting DXFs and editable source links. The digital check found 17 valid solids with no solid overlaps, but that does not replace checking the real parts.

There were a few problems to sort out. Some retainer clearances needed correcting, the CNC and printed files had to be put in the right groups, and Half Life flagged that STEP alone was not editable source. Adding the native Onshape links to the project description cleared that check. The deep frame is a 3D CNC milling job; the flat DXFs alone cannot make the whole case.

The perfboard schematic has a clean electrical check, and the ESP32 firmware compiles. The code includes local text/animation controls and microphone input. I have not powered a panel or tested the circuit physically, and Spotify is still a future feature. The panel scan setup needs checking before enabling display output.

I checked the carts, added the microphone and mounting hardware, allowed 2m each of red and black power wire, and saved screenshots. The carts total Rs 4,603, including the displayed buffer-chip delivery. My budget is now Rs 6,445 including delivery. CNC work, printing, remaining delivery and final mounting/power protection still need pricing, so the remaining Rs 1,842 is not all upgrade money.

Tomorrow I want to get the CNC quote and confirm the actual panel and power-supply dimensions, connectors and cable space. After those costs are covered, I can consider automatic brightness and buttons. Nothing has been ordered yet.
